messages:
Alex M: Quick Q — where are the panels that show per-model prefix hit-rate + eviction rates? Trying to tune the prod-prefetch alert thresholds before next deploy.
Priya S: Grafana folder: /dashboards/infra/cache/prefix-hit-rate. direct link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/prefix-cache?orgId=1&from=now-1h :eyes:
Sam R: The single-panel % hit rate by model is called \"Prefix hit % (5m)\". There's also a companion panel \"Prefetch evictions/sec\" on the same row.
Tina L: If you want PromQL for use in alerts, this is what we use currently:
```promql
100 * sum by (model) (increase(kv_prefix_hits_total[5m]))
/ sum by (model) (increase(kv_prefix_requests_total[5m]))
```
Priya S: for evictions:
```promql
sum by (model) (increase(kv_prefix_evictions_total[5m]))
```
Alex M: Nice. Is there an existing alert rule to tweak, or should I make a new one? Current prod alert fires a lot early-morning and is noisy.
Sam R: There's an alert rule `PrefixCacheLowHitrate` in prometheus/alerts/cache.rules. It currently fires when 5m hit% < 60 for any model for 3m. That's probably too aggressive for low-traffic models.
Tina L: Proposed change: only alert if 5m hit% < 60 AND requests/sec > 0.2 (to ignore tiny models), and keep for 10m. That reduces noise. Example rule expression:
```yaml
expr: (
  (100 * sum by(model)(increase(kv_prefix_hits_total[5m]))
   / sum by(model)(increase(kv_prefix_requests_total[5m]))) < 60
) and (sum by(model)(increase(kv_prefix_requests_total[10m])) > 120)
for: 10m
```
Sam R: That second clause means >120 requests in 10m (~0.2 rps) — seems reasonable.
Priya S: Also add a suppression for models in the `dev-*` org label, they cause a lot of noise. We tag with `org` label in metrics.
Alex M: Good call. I'll draft a PR against infra/monitoring with updated rule + change log. @Tina L can you review the alert expression and wording? :pray:
Tina L: Yep, can review. Also add a runbook link in the alert with steps: check panel, check recent deploys, check model rollout tags.
Alex M: What runbook do we reference? I can't find the cache runbook.
Sam R: Runbook: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/cache-prefetch.md — includes quick checks and common mitigation (rollback, bump prefetch budget, temporary fallback to LRU).
grafana-bot: Panel snapshot created by Priya S: https://grafana.redwood.com/dashboard/snapshot/xyz789
Alex M: One more question — where do we see sample traces when hit% drops? I'd like a trace that shows KV miss path.
Priya S: Traces are in Tempo. Search span name `kv.prefix.lookup` and filter by `model=` label. Example: https://tempo.redwood.com/trace?service=inference&span=kv.prefix.lookup&from=now-1h
ops-bot: Noted. I'll update the alert in staging when PR lands and run a canary for 24h.
Alex M: Thanks — I'll open the PR now and ping here when ready. :thumbsup:
Tina L: Quick note for the PR: include the Grafana panel ids you looked at and screenshot of expected reduction in noise (e.g., last 7 days comparison).
Alex M: Will do. PR: infra/monitoring#452
Sam R: @Alex M — cc @oncall-cache when you merge so we can watch the new rule.
Alex M: Will do. Thread locking for visibility: leaving the dashboard link in comments so others can find it later.
